words.gloss_range: restrictive and assertive opening particle; locally frames the following promised content as the focused proposition being validated
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innamā}}) opens 51:5 as the answer to the oath sequence, not as another suspended oath. Its payoff is restrictive as well as assertive: the promised matter is gathered into one focused proposition and set against rival accounts of the addressed future, while the local grammar keeps that exclusivity tied to this promise clause rather than to every possible truth claim. The fused particle also lets the reader hear compression at the start: assertion, restriction, and launch-position arrive in one word before the passive promise opens out.

topics.headline: restrictive scope over promised content
topics.summary: The particle combines assertion and restriction, focusing the following promised matter as the proposition validated by the clause.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is not only affirming the promise but restricting the truth-focus to the promised matter against rival accounts of the addressed future.
topics.reason: The restrictive-particle analysis is locally licensed, but the broad only-true wording is narrowed to the promise field governed by the clause.

topics.headline: fused particle and relative subject frame
topics.summary: The written fusion can be read as a compact restrictive particle or as an assertion plus relative segment, with the same local result: the promised content becomes the subject-like unit predicated as true.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Arabic compresses assertion, restriction, and the what-is-promised subject frame into one opening surface.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence supports the relative segment as denoting promised content while QAC supports the fused restrictive particle surface.

topics.headline: oath answer begins here
topics.summary: The opening position turns the four-oath preamble into a declarative answer.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speech-act turn at 51:5: the prior oath sequence resolves into conclusion-delivery at this first word.
topics.reason: The context window identifies 51:5 as following the coordinated oaths of 51:1-4, so the launch-position claim is retained as structural payoff.

topics.headline: nasal and geminated opening pressure
topics.summary: The opening sound pattern tightens the restrictive launch and links the assertion acoustically to the later passive ending and predicate close.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening is not only grammatical; its doubled nasal pressure and later nasal recurrence make the assertion feel tightly bound across the ayah.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local to the surface and does not overrule syntax, so it remains a candidate acoustic payoff.

words.gloss_range: you are being promised or warned; local passive imperfect makes the addressees recipients while leaving promiser and object unstated
words.root_gloss_range: promise, threat, appointment, mutual promising, and promising sign branches; this occurrence activates the promise or warning commitment branch while local grammar blocks mutual appointment and concrete sign branches
words.prose: {{ar:تُوعَدُونَ}} ({{tr:tūʿadūna}}) makes the audience grammatically present as the recipients of the promise while suppressing the promiser. Its imperfect passive form keeps the address live and renewed, not a closed report about a past promise. The relative promise clause becomes the subject being judged, and the missing object is a major payoff: promise and warning remain held together under one future commitment, so the ayah validates the whole promise-field before 51:6 narrows the field toward judgment/recompense. The same passive promise form also becomes a local thread later in the surah (51:22; 51:60), while the promise-truth challenge field is answered here as a verdict rather than left as a question. The sound of the long vowel lets the promise stretch before the compact truth predicate closes it.

topics.headline: passive direct address foregrounds recipients
topics.summary: The second-person plural passive makes the addressees recipients of a promise while the promiser remains unexpressed.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audience is inside the verb as the affected party, while the source of the promise is deliberately left unspoken.
topics.reason: The passive 2mp morphology and attachment evidence support recipient foregrounding and agent suppression.

topics.headline: imperfect form renews the promise
topics.summary: The imperfect passive presents the promise as an ongoing address rather than a completed past report.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recited line re-addresses its hearers with the promise it describes.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the form as imperfect, so the rows' ongoing-address payoff can stand without treating it as a completed perfect.

topics.headline: object omission leaves promise and warning open
topics.summary: The objectless passive compresses the promised content, allowing favorable promise and threat-pressure to remain open until the next ayah gives surface uptake.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah validates a broad promised future before specifying any single reward or punishment, with 51:6 beginning the narrowing toward judgment/recompense.
topics.reason: The verb has no retained object locally, but the threat-color from Form IV is narrowed so it does not name a specific punishment or exclude favorable promise.

topics.headline: promise root makes the future a commitment
topics.summary: The root field gives the future content the force of a pledged outcome, not a loose prediction.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the predicate judges a committed future outcome, not a casual forecast.
topics.reason: V4 supports promise and threat branches for the root, and the local passive objectless frame keeps that future commitment compressed.

topics.headline: promise clause becomes the subject
topics.summary: The relative promise clause functions as the grammatical entity judged by the predicate.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is judged true is the promised content itself, not an incidental subordinate detail.
topics.reason: The relative segment attached to the opening particle supplies the content that the final predicate evaluates.

topics.headline: promise-truth thread and later returns
topics.summary: The passive promise wording participates in a local surah thread and in a broader promise-truth association, while the local ayah remains the controlling parse.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the open promise of 51:5 is not isolated: later promise returns in 51:22 and 51:60 reprise the field without replacing the local openness.
topics.reason: The rows' recurrence and cooccurrence payoff is retained, but narrowed so later references illuminate rather than determine the local objectless passive.

topics.headline: oath scene turns into direct address
topics.summary: The transition from the preceding oath imagery into second-person passive address makes the promised matter bear directly on the addressees.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary move from cosmic witness-language into a claim laid directly on the hearers.
topics.reason: The second-person passive creates a local grammatical shift from the preceding oath scene into addressed promise.

topics.headline: cadence stretches before predicate closure
topics.summary: The long vowel and nasal recurrence audibly extend the promise before the compact truth predicate closes the ayah.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an acoustic movement from stretched passive reception into a clipped verdict.
topics.reason: The cadence claim is kept as a surface-level payoff and does not control lexical sense.

topics.headline: promise-truth challenge answered
topics.summary: The promise-truth field is presented here as a verdict rather than a question.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a challenge field about whether the promise is true is turned into a direct answer.
topics.reason: The cooccurrence and form-class rows support a promise-truth association, while the local clause supplies the declarative verdict.

words.gloss_range: prefixed emphatic particle on the predicate; locally marks both predicate certainty and oath-answer force
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la-}}) is small but decisive because it attaches the oath answer to the predicate itself. It does not create a second proposition; it scopes certainty onto the truth predicate and makes the prior oath sequence grammatically land here. Its hinge position also keeps the promised-content subject from floating: the reader is carried from the relative promise clause into a compact nominal assertion with no overt copula.

topics.headline: certainty scoped onto predicate
topics.summary: The prefixed particle intensifies the predicate without adding a separate proposition.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that certainty is bound to the truth predicate itself, not added as a loose adverbial comment.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence both place the particle on the predicate, preserving local emphatic scope.

topics.headline: grammatical trace of oath answer
topics.summary: The particle carries the response force of the preceding oath series into the current predicate.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the link to 51:1-4 is grammatical, not merely thematic.
topics.reason: The context window and emphatic-predicate evidence license the particle as the marker by which the oath sequence resolves.

topics.headline: hinge into compact nominal predication
topics.summary: The particle directs the relative promise subject into the predicate and completes the nominal assertion.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the promised-content clause becomes a complete assertion only when this particle turns into the predicate.
topics.reason: The local syntax supports a nominal predication in which the particle-bearing predicate completes the frame.

words.gloss_range: truthful, true, and proving true; locally an active-participle predicate asserting the promised matter as truth-bearing and realized
words.root_gloss_range: truth in speech, firmness, true worth, confirmation and fulfillment, sincerity, charity, and dower branches; local predicate activates truth, fulfillment, and firmness pressures while non-predicate branches remain only family resonance
words.prose: {{ar:صَادِقٌۭ}} ({{tr:ṣādiqun}}) is the ayah's landing word: the oath sequence, restriction, passive promise, and emphatic particle all resolve in this predicate. As a nominative predicate in a nominal frame, it states a stable truth-quality rather than narrating an event; as an active participle, it does more than say the promise has been externally verified, casting the promised matter as truth-bearing in itself. The root payoff is twofold and must stay visible: truth includes fulfillment of a promise, as in the promise-proved-true association (39:74; 46:16), and it also carries firmness, so the promised matter lands as solid and resistant to collapse. Sincerity, charity, friendship, and dower branches are narrowed to family resonance rather than literal local senses, and the promise itself receives the verdict rather than human challengers or a rival reality-register. The final indefinite cadence and heavy consonant texture seal the assertion and anticipate the next ayah's occurring-verdict (51:6), while a non-canonical specifying addition only highlights how open the canonical promise remains.

topics.headline: final predicate as oath-response landing
topics.summary: The last word carries the semantic and grammatical payoff of the oath answer.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole oath-response movement lands on this final truth predicate.
topics.reason: The word is the predicate of the opened clause and the final semantic terminus of the oath answer.

topics.headline: active participle makes the promise truth-bearing
topics.summary: The form attributes active truth-quality to the promised matter rather than merely presenting it as externally certified.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promise itself is made the bearer of truth, not only the object of outside verification.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an active participle predicate, supporting the row's contrast with a passive verified form.

topics.headline: nominal predicate states stable truth
topics.summary: The predicate is nominative within a nominal frame, giving a stable identity-quality rather than narrating an event.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah states the promised matter as true in a stable predication rather than reporting an event happening.
topics.reason: Local syntax identifies this word as the nominative predicate of the nominal construction.

topics.headline: truth includes promised realization
topics.summary: The truth predicate carries correspondence and fulfillment together, so the promised future is judged as a realized-outcome claim.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that true here is not bare truthful speech; it includes the promise proving true in realization, with 39:74 and 46:16 illustrating the promise-truth pairing.
topics.reason: V4 supports both truth-in-speech and fulfillment branches, and the local promise verb makes fulfillment a direct reader payoff.

topics.headline: firmness hardens the truth claim
topics.summary: The root's firmness image makes the abstract truth claim feel solid, while the local predicate remains a truth and fulfillment predicate rather than a literal hard object.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promised matter is presented as firm and resistant to collapse, not merely correct as wording.
topics.reason: V4 supports a firmness branch for the root, but local predication narrows it to image-pressure inside truth language.

topics.headline: sincerity family colors commitment
topics.summary: Truth-family branches such as charity, friendship, and dower are not literal local senses, but they support sincerity and enacted commitment as family resonance.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a sincerity-and-enacted-commitment coloring around the promise, while avoiding a literal charity, friendship, or dower reading.
topics.reason: The wider root family is valid as semantic background, but local predicate grammar blocks literal activation of charity, friendship, and dower branches.

topics.headline: non-canonical specification highlights openness
topics.summary: A non-canonical specifying addition is useful only as contrast: the canonical wording leaves the promised content open.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that canonical 51:5 does not specify the promise referent at the predicate; its openness is part of the surface.
topics.reason: The qiraat row is kept only as contrast and does not govern the canonical local parse.

topics.headline: attached emphasis and final cadence seal the predicate
topics.summary: The attached emphatic particle and final tanwin make the predicate a single recited unit of closure, with cadence linking truth to the next ayah's occurrence statement.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sound and surface shape seal the predicate, then acoustically bind true in 51:5 to occurring in 51:6.
topics.reason: The affixal and cadence rows describe local surface effects and the adjacent 51:6 closure without altering syntax.

topics.headline: truth verdict redirects challenge and oath pressure
topics.summary: The predicate turns surrounding promise-challenge and oath-pressure fields into a declarative verdict on the promise itself.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promise itself, rather than challengers or rival reality language, receives the active truth verdict.
topics.reason: The cooccurrence and challenge-formula rows survive as corpus-field payoff, while the local active-participle predicate remains controlling.

topics.headline: heavy consonants weight the truth predicate
topics.summary: The emphatic opening consonant and stop texture give the final predicate acoustic weight matching its firm truth claim.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the predicate's sound profile reinforces its semantic gravity at the close.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is retained as local sound payoff and does not introduce a new lexical sense.

topics.headline: oath pressure resolves as truth declaration
topics.summary: The preceding oath register supplies pressure that resolves in this compact truth declaration.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from sworn witness-language into a final declarative verdict.
topics.reason: The boundary-register row is locally supported by the context window and by the predicate's final position.

1. **Promise as already moving into fulfillment.** `و ع د/B001` supplies a spoken promise opening expectation and `ص د ق/B004` confirmation/fulfillment. The staged operations of 51:1-4 precede the claim, while 51:60 repeats the promised day. The packet supplies expectation and fulfillment; I infer **ordered execution already underway -> promise confirmed in event**. *Ṣādiq* thus reads dynamically as realization, not only truthfulness.
2. **Promise and threat remain simultaneous.** `و ع د/B002` accepts a threat toward harm, activated by the fire scene (51:13-14) and final woe (51:60), while 51:15-19 activates promised benefit. I infer **one appointment -> divergent outcomes by recipient**. The verse should preserve beneficent promise and punitive threat rather than collapse them.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The split between 51:15-19 and 51:60 prevented *tūʿadūn* from resolving into only good promise or only threat; both remain active under one fulfillment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Truth as fulfillment already modeled by process.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `و ع د/B006` is “a promising sign of what is expected,” and fixed `ص د ق/B004` is “confirmation and fulfillment.” **Structural cue:** 51:1–4 supply an ordered material analogy, separating, bearing, conveying, and assigning, while 51:6 names occurrence; 51:8–10 then oppose this order with divergent speech, diversion, and conjectural estimating. **Role and abduction:** the oath sequence acts as the sign and fulfillment is its terminus; I infer that the visible coherence of the sequence warrants expectation before the outcome arrives. **Reading change:** “true” becomes performative and processual: what is promised is already showing the structure by which it will be fulfilled.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:6 supplied the immediate terminus, while 51:8–10’s divergent conjecture clarified that `ص د ق/B004` concerns reliable fulfillment rather than one more competing statement.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, gözle görülür belirtilerden toprak, gün, hayvan veya insan hakkında gelecek bir durumun beklenmesini ortaklaştırır. Beklenen şey her zaman iyilik değildir; günün başlangıcı sıcaklık ya da soğukluk gösterebildiği için çekirdek, olumlu umut yerine belirtiye dayalı gelecek beklentisi olarak kurulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel niteleme ile toprak, gün, hayvan ve insan belirtilerine bağlı kuruluşlar ayrı örnekler olarak korunur; bunlardan sözlü söz verme anlamı çıkarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlıkta veya durumun başlangıcında görülen belirtilerin, gelecekte ortaya çıkacak bir özellik ya da sonuç için beklenti doğurmasıdır. Toprağın yağmur ve bitki, günün sıcaklık veya soğukluk, hayvanın gelişme, insanın da huy bakımından değerlendirilmesi bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Şimdiki belirtiler, gelecekte ortaya çıkacak bir durum, özellik veya sonuç için beklenti doğurur.

Günün başlangıcı, ilerleyen saatlerde sıcaklık veya soğukluk görüleceğini gösterebilir.
Bir hayvanın belirtileri, ondan iyilik veya olumlu gelişme bekleneceğini gösterebilir.
Bir insanın görünür belirtileri, cömertlik, dayanıklılık veya kararlılık gibi huyların beklendiğini gösterebilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi fiziksel bir şey için sertlik ve düz ya da düzgün olma niteliklerini açıkça birlikte verir; mızrak örneği de bu somut nitelemeyi destekler. Dalın fiziksel güç ve biçim düzgünlüğü çerçevesi bu kanıtla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal söz doğruluğunu veya ahlaki güvenilirliği değil, bir nesnenin somut sertlik ve düzgünlük niteliğini anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın nitelik sertlik ya da düzgünlük olarak tanımlanır; nesne ve mızrakla kurulan niteleme örnekleri yalnızca bu fiziksel anlamın yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

concept_map.definition: Bir nesnenin fiziksel olarak sert ve dayanıklı ya da biçim bakımından düz ve düzgün olmasıdır.

facets.statement: Nesne fiziksel sertlik ve sağlamlık taşır.
Nitelik, biçim bakımından düz veya düzgün olmayı da anlatabilir.
Sert ve güçlü bir mızrak bu fiziksel niteliğin örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak kanıt, fiziksel nesneyi sert ve sağlam diye niteler; bazı aktarımlar buna düz veya düzgün olma yönünü de ekler ve mızrağı örnek verir.

error_profile.preserves: Sertlik ve düzgünlük yönlerini alternatif fiziksel nitelikler olarak korur.

error_profile.loses: Düz veya düzgün biçimli olma seçeneğini karşılamaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi insan nitelemelerini, herhangi bir şeyde tamlık fikrini ve övgüye uygun sağlam durum bildiren bir dizi kullanımı aynı dalda toplar. Verilen tam iyilik ve kalıcılık çerçevesi, bu kullanımları söz doğruluğuna indirgemeden bir arada tutar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, yalnızca doğru haber vermeyi değil; bir kişi, şey veya durumdaki tamlık, iyilik, güvenilirlik ve övgüye değer sağlamlığı anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçimdeki tamlık anlamı korunur; kişi nitelemeleri ile yer, öncelik, giriş, çıkış ve anılma alanındaki yapıya bağlı övgü kullanımları ayrı yüzler olarak gösterilir.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi, şey veya durumun iyi, güvenilir ve övgüye değer sayılacak ölçüde tam ve sağlam olmasıdır. Kişi nitelemelerinde erdem ve güvenilirlik, belirli yapılarda ise kalıcı ve övülebilir bir durum öne çıkar.

facets.statement: Bir şey kendi türü içinde tamlığa ve kusursuzluğa erişmiştir.
İnsan nitelemesinde iyilik, erdem, sağlam karakter ve güvenilirlik öne çıkar.
Yer, öncelik, giriş, çıkış veya anılma gibi alanlarda durumun iyi, sağlam ve sonradan övülmeye elverişli oluşunu belirtir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, tamlığı genel çekirdek olarak verir; insanları iyilik ve güvenilirlikle niteler, belirli durumları da doğru biçimde övülmeye elverişli sağlamlıkları bakımından değerlendirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Şeylerdeki kusursuzluğu, kişilerdeki erdemi ve durumlarda övgüye değer sağlamlığı birlikte temsil eden üst karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Tamlık çekirdeğini, olumlu değerlemeyi ve güvenilir sağlamlık yönünü birlikte korur.

error_profile.loses: Şeylerdeki genel tamlığı ve durumlara bağlı övgü kullanımlarını kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir yerin, başlangıcın, girişin, çıkışın veya kalıcı anılmanın iyi ve övgüye uygun niteliği anlatıldığında kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnızca vaat veya savaşta gereğini yapmayı değil, bir tahmini gerçekleştirmeyi, bir sözü onaylamayı ve önceki bir bildiriyi destekleyip doğrulamayı da kapsar. Bu nedenle dal, salt vaat yerine getirme olarak değil; söz, beklenti veya iddiayı gerçekleşme, eylem ya da onayla doğrulama alanı olarak yeniden çerçevelenmelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Fiilî yerine getirme çekirdeğin önemli bir görünümüdür; ancak gerçekleşen tahmin ve doğrulayıcı onay da dalın sınırı içinde kalır.

facets.statement: Bir söz, beklenti veya iddia gerçekleşme, eylem ya da onayla doğru çıkarılır.

Bir tahminin veya beklentinin doğru çıkması da gerçekleşme yoluyla doğrulamadır.
Bir sözün doğruluğunu kabul etmek veya önceki bir bildiriyi desteklemek onay yoluyla doğrulamadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek, bir söz veya beklentinin eylemle, gerçekleşmeyle ya da onayla doğrulanmasıdır; savaşta gereğini yapma, tahminin çıkması ve önceki bildiriyi destekleme bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.
